title: How Raft replaces a failed leader
purpose: See how followers detect a dead leader, elect a new one with a majority of votes, and why a minority cannot make progress.
sequence_reason: Leader failure, election timeout, vote requests and the new term happen in a fixed causal order.
summary: A five-server Raft cluster loses its leader. Heartbeats stop, a follower's election timeout fires, it becomes a candidate for term 2 and asks for votes. With three of five votes it becomes leader. When only two servers are alive, no candidate can reach a majority, so the cluster stops accepting writes.
explanation: A leader rules only while a majority hears it. A new leader needs votes from a majority of all servers, so two leaders can never win the same term.

learning_check.question: Five servers, three of them are down. Can the two live servers elect a leader?
learning_check.answer: No. A leader needs votes from a majority of all five servers, which is three, and only two can vote.

scenes.heading: When the leader fails
scenes.narration: What happens when the Raft leader crashes?

visual.subtitle: Heartbeats, timeouts, votes, a new term

scenes.heading: The leader sends heartbeats
scenes.narration: While it is alive, the leader sends heartbeats to the followers. Each heartbeat resets their election timers.

scenes.heading: Heartbeats stop, a timeout fires
scenes.narration: The leader crashes and the heartbeats stop. Election timeouts are random, so one follower times out first and becomes a candidate.

items: S2 becomes a candidate for term 2

scenes.heading: The candidate asks for votes
scenes.narration: The candidate votes for itself and sends RequestVote to the others. Each server votes once per term. Three votes of five make it leader.

path.label: Three of five votes: S2 leads term 2

scenes.heading: A minority cannot elect
scenes.narration: If only two of five servers are alive, no candidate gets three votes. There is no leader, so no write commits.

visual.verdict: Safety first: no majority, no progress.
